projects.title: 3000 Sq Ft Modern Classical Interior Apartment, Basabo, Dhaka
projects.description:
Perched on the ninth floor of a quiet address in Basabo, Sabujbagh, this 3,000 square foot residence was designed around one clear idea: a white themed home that feels elegant without ever feeling cold. The family wanted classic character with the ease of modern living, so we built the whole apartment on a warm white palette and layered it with brass detailing, marble surfaces and soft, warm tone lighting. The result is a home that reads bright and airy through the day and turns intimate and golden after dark.

Every room was planned as part of one visual language. Fluted and channel tufted textures repeat from the living room to the bedrooms, gold and brass fixtures tie the spaces together, and cove lighting traces the ceilings so the light always feels built in rather than added on. This is what modern classical interior design looks like when it is done for the way people actually live.

The heart of the apartment is a single open plan volume where the living, dining and kitchen flow together under wide archways and a coffered ceiling. We centred the dining zone on a white marble table framed by cream and charcoal upholstered chairs, then hung a brass five arm chandelier alongside a slim crystal pendant to give the room both sparkle and warmth. Glass front china cabinets in white display the family’s dishware, while a green and gold marbled canvas and a framed turquoise ocean wave photograph add quiet colour against the white walls.

Turn toward the living room and the feature wall does the talking. We wrapped the television in a wavy, ribbed three dimensional panel, flanked it with brass wall sconces and floated a white console beneath it. Beige sofas layered with burgundy and charcoal cushions sit on a patterned grey rug, and gold ring chandeliers and a mirror collage keep the eye moving across the double height sitting space. Bronze ceiling fans and large format grey floor tile run throughout, so the whole common area feels connected and calm.

The master suite continues the warm white theme in beige and taupe. A vertical channel tufted headboard anchors the bed, framed by geometric textured wall panels and matching sconces, with white nightstands and gold hardware on either side. Twin bronze ceiling fans sit in a coffered ceiling above floor to ceiling curtains layered over sheers.

projects.title: 1600 Sq Ft Modern Interior Apartment, Uttara Sector 6
projects.description:
This 1,600 square foot apartment on Road 10, Plot 19 in Uttara Sector 6 was designed as a bright, modern family home where every piece of furniture was drawn for the space. Working across interior design, lighting design and custom furniture design, we kept the palette clean and white, layered in fluted wood panelling and warm brass detailing, and gave each room a clear purpose, from a dedicated prayer room to a playful loft bedroom for the children.

The home proves that a compact footprint can still feel generous. Custom cabinetry, built in seating and made to measure wardrobes let us use every corner, while crystal chandeliers, brass fans and cove lighting keep the whole apartment feeling warm and elegant.

The living room is wrapped in fluted vertical wood panelling, with a backlit arched niche framing botanical mural artwork. We designed the cream sofa set, a three seater plus a loveseat, and dressed it with burgundy and grey cushions around a two tone coffee table. A ribbed texture TV feature wall with a floating console and chrome sconces anchors the lounge, lit from above by brass ceiling fans and a crystal chandelier.

The dining area sits just beyond, finished with coffered grid wall panelling and a custom marble top waterfall table surrounded by cream and grey upholstered chairs with gold capped legs. A crystal drum chandelier hangs above, and a pass through connects to white glass front display cabinetry, marble counters and under cabinet lighting, so the cooking, dining and living spaces read as one continuous, sociable floor.

The master bedroom centres on a diamond quilted upholstered accent wall behind a custom channel tufted headboard in soft taupe grey. Along one wall we built a six bay white wardrobe with carved sunburst medallion panels and brass bar pulls. An arched mirror nook with backlit shelving and brass candle style sconces adds depth, while a dedicated dressing zone with an arched window seat, a gold framed mirror and a custom vanity console turns getting ready into a calm daily ritual.

projects.title: 3000 Sq Ft Modern Classical Interior Apartment, Gulshan 2
projects.description:
This 3,000 square foot apartment at 5/A, Road 94 in Gulshan 2 was designed as a polished modern classical home where white joinery, gold inlay detailing and warm tone lighting come together across a generous floor plan. The brief called for understated luxury, so we kept the palette light and consistent, then used gold strip inlays, fluted panelling and layered lighting to give every room a quiet sense of occasion.

With a formal living room, a family lounge, a dining area, a full kitchen, four bedrooms and an en suite, the apartment was planned for a family that entertains as easily as it relaxes. Warm cove lighting runs through the ceilings so the home glows gently after dark, exactly as the lighting design brief intended.

The common area is built around two distinct moods. The formal living room opens with an arched gold framed mirror and a hanging disc screen at the entry, then settles into a taupe L shaped sectional around a black coffee table and a pouf ottoman. A white fluted TV feature wall with a floating console anchors one end, a round crystal and gold ring pendant lights the centre, and an abstract green and gold marbleized canvas adds colour against the pale panelling.

Just beyond, the family lounge is softer and more relaxed, with a grey and white marble accent wall opening onto a kitchen pass through lined with pendant lights and bar stools. The formal dining area seats the family in gold X frame upholstered chairs beneath a gold ring chandelier, next to a gallery wall of framed photographs. The U shaped kitchen carries glass front upper cabinets and a waterfall edge marble island with warm wood slat cladding, so cooking stays connected to the life of the home.

The master bedroom sits against a grey fabric headboard wall detailed with vertical gold metal strip inlays and white fluted pilasters, lit by cream wall sconces and a gold cove ceiling. The suite flows into its own dressing room, wrapped in floor to ceiling white wardrobes with gold strip inlays, gold pulls and a keypad locked door for security. A vanity with a round gold sunburst mirror completes the space, and the same green and gold marbleized artwork ties the suite back to the living areas.

projects.title: 2000 Sq Ft Modern Interior Apartment, Bashundhara R/A Block-M
projects.description:
This 2,000 square foot apartment on Road 16 and 17 in Bashundhara R/A, Block-M was designed as a bright, modern family home with a clean white base and just enough pattern to give it life. The brief asked for a minimal, elegant look, so we kept surfaces white and calm, then layered in floral branch murals, faceted wall panels and gold detailing to keep the home warm and characterful rather than clinical.

The apartment was planned for a growing family, with a restful master suite, a separate parents room, and two very different children’s bedrooms. Custom cabinetry and built in joinery run through every space, so storage feels designed in rather than added on.

The living and dining areas connect through white panelled glass French doors over large format grey floor tile, so the whole social heart of the home reads as one open space. In the lounge we set a white three dimensional geometric tile panel behind the television, balanced across the room by cream and gold leaf pattern wallpaper and clusters of gold hexagon mirrors. Beige sofas and a houndstooth accent chair sit around low trays and a round coffee table.

The dining zone centres on a marble top table with grey upholstered chairs beneath a gold branch crystal chandelier, with glass front white cabinetry displaying dishware and pantry jars along the wall. We added quieter moments too, an arched wallpaper nook with a built in cushioned bench, and a reading corner with a backlit bookshelf niche and a grey swivel armchair, while a floral branch mural with a copper disc sculpture gives the space its signature wall.

The master bedroom keeps the palette soft and minimal. A taupe headboard wall carries a gold sunburst mirror above a channel tufted greige headboard, and a floor to ceiling white wardrobe with fluted base panels, gold hardware and a smoked glass centre section handles storage without visual clutter. A round gold framed mirror hangs over a floating vanity with gold knob drawers, and a corner study desk with backlit shelving rounds out the suite. Charcoal bedding with a rust throw keeps the room grounded against the pale walls.

projects.title: 2000 Sq Ft Modern Classical Interior Apartment, Bashundhara R/A Block-L
projects.description:
This 2,000 square foot apartment on Road 11 in Bashundhara R/A, Block-L was designed as a modern classical home where crisp white surfaces meet warm gold detailing and honest marble. The brief was timeless elegance that still feels current, so we built the whole home on a white palette, layered in raised panel wainscoting and fluted wall treatments, and let brushed gold fixtures carry the classic character from the entrance through every bedroom.

Marble runs as a thread through the apartment, from accent walls with soft grey veining to waterfall counters and dining tops, while gold ring chandeliers, crystal fixtures and slim wall sconces keep the light warm. The result is refined without being formal, a home that looks composed and lives comfortably.

The living and dining zone is the showpiece. We defined it with raised panel white wainscoting, a white marble accent wall with grey veining, and a fluted feature wall for the television. A white fretwork lattice divider with glass shelves and backlit niches separates the living and dining areas without closing them off, so light and sightlines carry across the floor.

Beige sofas and swivel armchairs with charcoal cushions sit on soft grey rugs around nested marble top tables, while an oval marble dining table with taupe upholstered gold leg chairs anchors the dining side beneath a gold ring chandelier and a crystal fixture. A tall built in display wall of backlit cubbies gives the family a curated place for vases, books and objects, and marble tile flooring ties every zone together.

The kitchen pairs light grey shaker cabinetry with brushed gold bar pulls and a marble waterfall island fronted with a warm wood slat detail. A cluster of frosted glass teardrop pendants on brass stems hangs over the island, glass front upper cabinets display white dishware under warm lighting, and a built in oven and microwave stack sits alongside side by side refrigerators. Marble counters, backsplash and flooring keep the room bright and cohesive with the rest of the home.

projects.title: Luxury Dining Room Design in Gulshan 2, 3000 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
Step in from the formal lounge and a marble topped table stands directly ahead of you, ringed with gold framed chairs and set under a shelf panel that runs the full width of the wall behind it. The table is laid with blue rimmed plates that match nothing else in sight. Nothing in the fixed scheme argues with them, which is the point of keeping the shell neutral.

Look right from the same spot and glass fronted crockery cabinets stand beside a painted forest panel with a gold ring chandelier over them. Look left and the room opens to the kitchen through a gold circle screen. Three of the four walls carry a different treatment, which sounds like too much until you notice that every piece of metal in all three is the same brushed gold.

The table top is a single marble slab with a squared edge, sat on a solid base rather than legs so chairs can be pushed in anywhere along its length. Gold frames on the chairs are slim enough that the top reads as the heavier object. A dining table is one of the few surfaces in a home that changes appearance every day, between breakfast, a work laptop and a full setting for fourteen, so nothing fixed around it was allowed to have an opinion about colour.

The same stone appears again as insets in the wardrobe doors of theluxury master bedroom design in Gulshan 2, cut from the same block so the veining runs on. That kind of carry through only works if the stone is bought once, at the start, for every room that needs it, rather than reordered in stages across a build.

Behind the table, gold shelf panelling is set into the wall with sconces mounted between the shelf runs. The shelves are shallow, sized for a bowl or a pair of objects rather than for books, and the sconces throw light sideways across them so each shelf has a lit face and a shadow under it. This is decorative joinery, not storage, doing the job a very large artwork would do in a different scheme.

projects.title: Modular Kitchen Design in Gulshan 2, 3000 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
Marble folds over both ends of the island and runs to the floor, mitred at the corner so the vein carries round without a visible joint. That waterfall detail is the most expensive centimetre of stone in the kitchen and the first thing anyone touches. It anchors an open cooking area inside a 3000 sq ft plan in Gulshan 2, where the kitchen is permanently in view from the dining table and had to be finished like a room rather than a service space.

There are two kitchens in this flat, and that is the fact everything else follows from. The open one you can see handles breakfast, serving and light cooking. A second, utility kitchen sits behind a frosted glass folding door and takes the heavy cooking, the double sink and the mess that comes with cooking Bengali food daily.

The cabinet run is a flat grey lacquer with no hardware showing on any front. Doors open on a routed finger pull along the top edge of the drawer bank and a push catch on the tall units. Handles are the first component that dates a kitchen visually, and in a kitchen this exposed to a dining room the absence of them keeps the run reading as panelling rather than as equipment.

The island carries the marble top over a grey carcass, with seating on the dining side and drawers on the cook side. A ring pendant hangs above it at 900mm off the stone, high enough to clear a sightline across the island and low enough to keep the light on the working surface instead of spreading it across the ceiling.

An induction hob sits in the marble on the open side under a black glass chimney hood, with a marble breakfast counter running behind it. Induction rather than gas was deliberate on this side. It puts out far less ambient heat, produces no combustion residue on nearby cabinet fronts, and can sit within a metre of where people are eating without turning that corner uncomfortable in May.

projects.title: Modern Family Living Room Design in Gulshan 2, 3000 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
The front of this flat was already committed to a formal lounge that nobody would relax in. That left one room to absorb everything the formal side could not take: a television on every night, homework at the same hour as the television, a ceiling fan running through summer and upholstery that gets sat on in outdoor clothes.

A second sitting room only works if it is given a different character rather than a smaller budget. This one drops the crystal and the gold panelling entirely, runs grey, and takes its cues from what an ordinary weekday evening in a large flat actually involves.

The first decision was to stop this room competing with the one at the front. No matched sofa set, no chandelier, no polished stone. Instead a deep grey sectional, artwork chosen for scale rather than for statement, and a ceiling that carries ring pendants at a normal height. A family room built as a scaled down version of a formal lounge always loses the comparison, and the household ends up using neither properly.

The test we apply is simple. If a family still drifts to the formal lounge a month after moving in, the second room was designed wrong. This one is planned so the pull runs the other way, which is exactly what the two room split in a large apartment is for. That whole arrangement is visible in thecommon space design serviceapproach we take to shared spaces.

A sectional was the only seat shape that could face two directions without cluttering the floor. The long run sits square to the wall mounted television, and the short return faces the dining and kitchen end, so somebody sitting there stays in conversation with whoever is cooking without turning round. An ocean canvas hangs above the long run and an abstract sits on the adjacent wall, both large enough to hold their walls without needing a second piece.

projects.title: Luxury Master Bedroom Design in Gulshan 2, 3000 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
Three requirements had to be satisfied here before a single elevation was worth drawing. Clothes had to live outside the sleeping area rather than along one wall of it. There had to be a place to sit and get ready that was not inside the wardrobe. And the room had to stay usable for sleep in the middle of a Dhaka afternoon, on a western elevation with full height glazing.

The first of those decided the layout on its own, because it meant finding the depth for a walk in dressing space in a plan that had not been drawn with one. That depth came from the corridor and the adjoining bathroom lobby, neither of which is space anybody sits down in.

What the bedroom got back is a sleeping area with almost no storage in it, which is the difference between a bedroom and a suite, and a scheme that could then run grey and white with gold inlay without competing with a wall of doors.

It is rare forbedroom interior design in Dhakato offer the depth for a dressing room, so when a plan turns out to have it we take it. The walk in is finished in fluted white with long gold handles and mirror strips set between the door runs, lit by a continuous cove rather than by spotlights. Cove lighting is the right answer in a wardrobe because it washes the full height of the hanging space evenly. A spotlight leaves the bottom half of a long garment in shadow, which is precisely where you are looking when you are choosing one.

Hanging heights are split, with full length on one side for saris and gowns and doubled shorter runs opposite. Drawer depths were set against what was going into them rather than against a standard, and the mirror strips let you check a hem inside the room instead of walking out to find a mirror.

projects.title: Luxury Girls Bedroom Design in Gulshan 2, 3000 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
Clothing in a teenager’s room roughly doubles between twelve and eighteen. A wardrobe sized for the child in the room on handover day is full within two seasons, and everything after that ends up on a chair. This room was drawn against the later number rather than the current one.

That decision produced an open walk in closet section instead of a standard four door unit, and it set the proportions of everything else on the wall. The palette runs beige and white with thin gold striping and brown curtains. There is no pink and nothing themed, because a themed room has to be redone in four years.

Before any joinery was drawn we counted what actually had to go in: hanging length in metres, folded stack heights, shoe pairs, bags, the winter things that only come out for two months. That audit is unglamorous and it is the whole design. Hanging heights allow full length dresses down one side and doubled shorter garments on the other, and each drawer depth was set by what was going into it rather than by a standard module. Counting first is the same habit that produced two kitchens rather than one in themodular kitchen design in Gulshan 2.

A wardrobe sized by allowance rather than by count is the most common failure in a child’s bedroom, and it shows up as an untidy room that everyone blames on the child. The same reasoning runs through ourbedroom interior design in Dhaka, applied at different ages and different budgets.

The wardrobe wall is white panelled with one section left open as a walk in closet. Open storage is a commitment, since it only ever looks good when it is kept in order, so the open bay is limited to hanging while every folded item lives behind a door. Nothing that gets stacked, and therefore nothing that gets messy, is on display.

projects.title: Luxury Guest Bedroom Design in Gulshan 2, 3000 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
Most Dhaka apartments hand the guest bedroom whatever is left over: the smallest room, one window facing a light well, a bed and a two door wardrobe bought at the end of the budget.

This flat does the opposite. The guest room takes the best aspect in the plan along with the most classical detailing anywhere in the apartment, and it reads as a room somebody designed rather than a room somebody filled.

That is a real trade rather than a flourish. A family bedroom gave up the cross light, and a room used a few weeks a year absorbed joinery detail that a daily room would have worn out. Neither half of that exchange is free.

Two windows light this room from different sides, which is unusual in a tower flat and is the reason it was picked as the guest room. Cross light makes a space feel welcoming in a way a single aspect never manages, and a visitor forms an opinion of a home from the room they wake up in. A family member gets to know the whole flat and can afford to sleep in a single aspect room. Across ourinterior design service in Gulshan, the guest bedroom is usually the one facing the light well, and it is usually the room that turns out to have been worth swapping.

The narrow strip of wall between the two windows would ordinarily be dead space, too tight for furniture and awkward to curtain. It carries a gold tile accent with a brass twin sconce mounted on it, which turns the plan’s most awkward dimension into the corner people notice first.

projects.title: Modern Living Room Design in Uttara Sector 6, 1600 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
Push the door open and a wall of vertical white fluting is what meets you, running floor to slab with a low cream sofa set against it. The second thing that registers is depth. Nothing tall stands between the threshold and the far window, so the room announces its full length in the first second, which is close to the only trick available to a living room in a flat of this size.

Every fixed element in here sits flat against a wall. That was settled at the elevation stage, before a single piece of loose furniture was chosen, because in 1,600 sq ft one cabinet projecting 400 mm into the walking route costs the room its whole character. What follows is the space in the order a visitor meets it, taken corner by corner from the entry door.

The opening render is shot from just inside the door, and it carries the two decisions that set everything after them. The fluting is a shallow half round rib repeated across the full wall height in flat white, which pulls the eye upward the way a picture rail used to. The sofa answers by staying low, so more of that ribbed surface stays visible above the cushion line. No rug was laid. The floor runs unbroken from the threshold to the far skirting, and an uninterrupted floor is worth more here than any amount of layering.

Turn a quarter left and the television wall arrives. Two renders frame it, one square on and one from the sofa’s own angle, and both show that the panel is a three dimensional wave relief rather than a printed board. The troughs run horizontally and change tone through the day as light crosses them. Below, a white console floats clear of the floor on concealed steel brackets, so the skirting line continues behind it and a mop passes underneath without anything being lifted.

Slim sconces sit either side of the panel at its own height rather than on the ceiling. Downlights would have washed the relief flat and left it reading as wallpaper. Light thrown sideways across a wave is what makes the shadow, and the shadow is the whole reason for specifying a moulded panel instead of paint. Goodliving room design in Dhakatends to hang on one wall doing more work than the others, and here that wall is the one the sofa faces.

projects.title: Modern Dining Room Design in Uttara Sector 6, 1600 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
One material rule runs through this room, which is that nothing dark sits at eye level. A heavy timber dining set does most of its damage after sunset, when it stops returning the little light a compact room has and starts swallowing it instead. So the finish list starts at white lacquer for the joinery, moves to marble for every working surface, and allows gold as the only visible metal.

Working from a fixed material list turns a room’s problems into fabrication problems, which are far easier to solve than taste problems. This room seats six, the household minimum, and it also carries the crockery for the entire flat because the kitchen beside it has none to spare. Shared function rooms make up the bulk of what we do undercommon space design service, and they are won or lost on the material schedule rather than on the layout.

A full height run of cabinetry occupies one long wall, sprayed white, with glass fronted uppers and solid lowers. It is built to the slab rather than stopped a foot below it, which removes the ledge that otherwise collects Dhaka dust and buys a full extra shelf for the things used twice a year. The carcass is board on a moisture resistant core, chosen for a city where a shut cabinet in June holds air at eighty per cent humidity. The same spray finish carries the pink arched doors in themodern kids bedroom design in Uttara Sector 6, so both rooms sit on one schedule.

Storage on this scale sits here because it cannot sit next door. Themodern kitchen design in Uttara Sector 6runs to two counter walls and no more, so the overflow was planned into this room from the first sketch instead of being discovered halfway through fit out.

The dining table is marble topped and sized for six, and a second marble run sits at waist height between the upper and lower cabinets, working as a serving counter through a meal. Real stone was used rather than an engineered surface because a slab was available locally at the length needed, and on the understanding that turmeric and lemon will mark it over the years. That is a condition of using stone, not a fault in it. Sealed twice a year it stays workable, and left alone it takes on a patina.

projects.title: Modern Kitchen Design in Uttara Sector 6, 1600 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
One window, one door, one gas line and a daily cooking load of heavy spice twice over. Those four constraints decided this kitchen before any drawing was started.

The room stays closed rather than opening onto the dining area, which in a flat of this size is the right answer far more often than the magazines suggest. An open kitchen in a flat of 1,600 sq ft carries the smell of a mustard oil tarka into every bedroom within minutes, and no extraction sold in Dhaka fixes that properly. A door is cheaper and it works.

A closed plan then has to earn itself back, because a shut kitchen in a small flat can turn into a cupboard. Everything inside works towards leaving the surfaces uninterrupted, with one continuous counter line, cabinet fronts carrying no projecting hardware, wall tiling in a single finish and every light source built into the joinery rather than hung from the ceiling. There is no pendant in here and nothing to duck around. Ourmodular kitchen design servicebegins from the same position on every compact flat we take on.

Cabinet fronts are grey and handleless, opening on a routed finger pull along the top edge of each door. In a galley this narrow that is a clearance decision rather than a styling one. A pull handle projects 30 to 40 mm into a walkway that is already tight, and it catches on kameez sleeves, bag straps and apron corners every time somebody passes behind the cook. Taking them off gives back close to 80 mm across the width of the room, which is one adult turning without contact.

The hob is gas and stays gas. Induction suits a different kind of cooking altogether, since the work this counter has to take runs on a high flame, heavy pans and a lot of dry roasting, and induction handles none of that well. Above it sits a black chimney hood sized wider than the hob itself. That single dimension is the most commonly ignored detail in a Bangladeshi kitchen and the one that decides whether the ceiling by the hob needs repainting every second year. Ducting was routed the shortest way to the external wall, with one bend rather than two.

projects.title: Modern Master Bedroom Design in Uttara Sector 6, 1600 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
Gold cup handles on white panelled doors, six sets of them in a line, are what the eye takes first here. They sit in a warm brass finish on a door module that repeats along the entire wall without a break. This is the master bedroom of a 1,600 sq ft apartment in Uttara Sector 6, and it had to hold two adults’ worth of clothing, a dressing station and somewhere to sit down, inside a footprint of no particular generosity.

Finishes are deliberately warmer and more classical than the rest of the flat. Channel tufting, brass, beige and layered sheers at the window, against the white lacquer and grey fluting that run everywhere else. A room the household retreats to at the end of a day is allowed to disagree with the apartment around it, and usually it should. Ourinterior design service in Uttaracovers several apartments where exactly one room is permitted to break the scheme on purpose.

A channel tufted headboard in pale fabric backs the bed, its channels running horizontally, and it is set into a wall panel carrying a diagonal lattice at a much larger scale. Two textures on one wall usually argue. These do not, because the scales are far apart and the directions cross, so the channels read as foreground and the lattice as a field behind them. That lattice is a relative of the carved screens in theprayer room and study design in Uttara Sector 6, drawn on the same geometric grid but left solid and painted out instead of being cut through.

Storage takes one long wall entirely, in classic white panelling with a brass sconce mounted at the end of the run. That brass is the same finish as the linear sconces in themodern dining room design in Uttara Sector 6, so the two rooms carry one warmth of metal between them and neither reads as a late addition. Inside, the wardrobe was divided from a count of what has to go into it rather than from a standard ratio, which is why one bay takes full length garments, two are shelved for folded stacks and the rest carry drawers on full extension runners.

Humidity settled the internals. Every bay is ventilated at the back and the base stands clear of the floor slab, because a sealed wardrobe in this city develops a smell by its second monsoon that no quantity of naphthalene solves. Doors are hinged rather than sliding, since a sliding pair always leaves half the storage shut, and there is just enough clearance at the foot of the bed to swing them. In practice,bedroom interior design in Dhakalives or dies on details of that kind rather than on door profiles.

projects.title: Modern Kids Bedroom Design in Uttara Sector 6, 1600 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
Two requirements had to be satisfied in this room and they pull in opposite directions. The structure has to read as a castle from the doorway, and it has to give back more storage than it takes out of the floor. A themed room that fails the second of those becomes a large pink object in a small bedroom inside a year, which is the usual fate of them.

So the bed was built rather than bought. A purchased bunk occupies volume and returns a mattress. A loft carpentered on site returns the stairs as drawers, the gable as shelving, the underside as a play den and the headboard wall as cubbies, all within the same footprint.

The loft is finished in soft pink and white with a brick patterned gable and an arched opening cut through it, and the render taken from the doorway shows it doing its job. From that angle the room is a castle and nothing else. Arched forms repeat elsewhere in this apartment, most obviously in the backlit lattice panel of theprayer room and study design in Uttara Sector 6, so the shape was already part of the flat’s vocabulary before it turned up here in pink.

It is built in moisture resistant board on a hardwood frame, with every exposed corner radiused and the guard rail set high enough to satisfy a parent watching from the door. Paint is a low odour water based system, which matters in a bedroom that stays shut through the worst of the summer. Nothing in the structure is hollow decoration either, since the gable itself is loadbearing and carries the shelves. The deck is set high enough that an adult stands under it without stooping, because a den you have to crouch in stops being used somewhere around the age of nine.

Every stair tread on the side access is a drawer front. Stairs took more width than a ladder would have and they earned it twice, once because a child climbing down at night is safer on a tread than a rung, and once because six drawers hold more than any toy box on the floor. Display shelving is set into the gable and lit from within, with cubby storage beside the padded headboard at the upper level.

projects.title: Modern Bedroom Design in Uttara Sector 6, 1600 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
Where the master bedroom takes every finish available to it, this second bedroom takes five. Grey fluting behind the bed, white panelled joinery, one gold sunburst, one ring pendant and a floating ledge. In most Dhaka flats the second bedroom becomes the room that absorbs whatever is left over, a spare television, a desk nobody uses and suitcases stacked on top of the wardrobe. This one was given two jobs, sleeping and dressing, and allowed to refuse everything else.

That refusal is what lets a modest room feel unhurried, and it is also what made it harder to get right. With five elements in a room, every one of them is visible. Rib spacing on the fluting, the diameter of the sunburst and the drop of the pendant were all settled on site with the pieces held up, not chosen off a supplier page. The study function this room does not carry was given a space of its own in theprayer room and study design in Uttara Sector 6, which is why nothing in here has to fold away or double up.

The headboard wall is fluted in grey, the only grey surface in an apartment otherwise held to white and cream. Convention says keep a small bedroom pale on the theory that pale reads larger. What pale actually delivers in a room taking hard morning light is a wall that throws it straight back at whoever is still asleep. Grey absorbs it. The room photographs slightly smaller and lives considerably better at half past six. The fluting runs floor to slab with no break at headboard height, so the wall stays one surface and the bed is simply parked against it. Vertical white ribs do the opposite job in themodern living room design in Uttara Sector 6, where the aim was height rather than quiet.

A single ring pendant hangs on one side of the bed, with a two drawer nightstand and a lamp point on the other. Matched pendants either side is the default, and it was wrong here, because the room is not symmetrical and forcing symmetry onto an asymmetric room shows immediately at the wall junctions. What was given up is the tidy look of a pair in a photograph. What was gained is a light on the side that actually gets read on, and a clear surface on the side that holds a phone and a glass of water.

Above the bed hangs a gold sunburst, the only ornament in the room and the only warm metal in it. Its finish was matched to the sconces in themodern dining room design in Uttara Sector 6so that a flat working with very few metals does not look like it changed its mind between rooms. One piece of wall art in a five element room has to be the right diameter, which is worth a full size template held against the wall before anything is fixed.

projects.title: Prayer Room and Study Design in Uttara Sector 6, 1600 Sq Ft Apartment
projects.description:
Light comes through a carved timber lattice before it reaches anything else in this room. The panel is arched, cut to a traditional geometric repeat and backlit from a cavity behind, so the pattern arrives as light rather than as relief. It belongs to a 1,600 sq ft flat in Uttara Sector 6, and it holds two functions at once, prayer on one side and study on the other.

Very few flats in Dhaka set aside a room for prayer, not because families do not want one but because the plan will not spare the area. Pairing it with a study is what made it affordable here in floor terms, and the two uses turn out to want the same conditions. It sits at the far end of the corridor from themodern kitchen design in Uttara Sector 6, which is the other reason it stays quiet through the evening.

The panel is timber, routed rather than laser cut, and the repeat was set out to a true traditional geometry instead of being approximated to fit the arch. That cost fabrication time and it is visible from a metre away, which is the distance the panel is actually looked at from when somebody is standing at it. Behind the lattice runs a 60 mm cavity holding a warm dimmable strip, diffused so no individual diode reads through the openings. At its lowest setting the panel glows and the rest of the room stays dark, which is how it gets used on most evenings.

Three circuits run in this room and each has its own switch. A crystal chandelier and a crystal bar fixture cover general light, a desk level circuit lights the working surface, and the cavity runs alone. Study wants a directed pool on the desk. Prayer wants even light with no shadow thrown across the floor. One circuit cannot deliver both, and a dual purpose room that tries reads as a compromise the moment anybody uses it. Under ourcommon space design service, a room asked to do two jobs gets separate switching or it ends up doing neither properly. Those crystal fixtures are smaller relatives of the chandelier hung over themodern living room design in Uttara Sector 6.

The floor changes material at the prayer side, from the apartment’s tiling to timber laid in a plain run. That change does the work a partition would have done, without the partition. It marks the threshold clearly enough that nobody walks onto it in outdoor slippers, it is warmer and quieter underfoot, and it leaves the space reading as one room rather than as two small ones with a wall between them. Carved geometric screens frame the same edge at head height, open enough to pass light and sound and definite enough to say where one function ends.

projects.title: Luxury Living Room Design in Basabo, Dhaka
projects.description:
Moulded wave panelling covers the television wall, sprayed the same warm white as the plaster beside it so the ripples register as shadow rather than as a second colour. From the sofa it is the first thing the eye lands on and the last thing to change when the lamps come on. The wall belongs to a 3,000 sq ft flat in Basabo, Dhaka, finished in the modern classical language the rest of the apartment follows. Warm white joinery, brushed gold metalwork, marble tile underfoot, very little else competing.

This is one long volume rather than a square room. It starts at the lobby door, carries along the television wall and stops only at the dining table, and protecting that single sightline decided the furniture plan before anything was chosen. Low sofa backs, a slim console, nothing tall anywhere along the run. The room is the second stop on the3,000 sq ft Basabo apartment project, and it is the one that sets the palette everything after it has to agree with.

The panels are moulded board, primed flat and sprayed after the ceiling was closed so no dust settled into a wet finish. The wave runs horizontally across a wall of roughly four metres, and the brass sconces on either side sit at eye height with their apertures aimed up and down instead of out. After dark the light rakes across the moulding and the relief looks twice as deep as it measures. At midday it flattens almost to nothing, which is the whole reason for using shadow instead of pigment.

Sconce centres were fixed on the drawing before panel widths were cut, because goodliving room design in Dhakalives or dies on that order of operations. Reverse it and a fitting lands on a crest instead of a trough, and every seat in the room can see the error. The screen is recessed into the panel field rather than hung over it, so the dark rectangle sits level with the crests when it is switched off.

Beneath the screen a white console spans the panelled recess with nothing touching the floor, carried on steel brackets fixed into the blockwork rather than on legs. Drawers are push to open, so no handle interrupts the front face, and they swallow remotes, cables and the router. A conduit inside the wall drops the television feed straight down into the cabinet, so not one lead is visible against the panelling. The IPS and the voltage stabiliser sit in the left hand section with the back panel cut away for airflow, which matters in a city where the mains fails several times a week and nobody wants to look at the box that covers for it.

projects.title: Luxury Dining Room Design in Basabo, Dhaka
projects.description:
One table here has to do three separate jobs. It feeds the family every day of the week, it absorbs the overflow when the front room fills with guests, and it forms the link between the living end of the flat and the kitchen. Rooms asked to do three things usually end up doing none of them properly.

In an apartment laid out as one continuous run, the specific risk was that the dining space would read as a wide corridor with furniture parked in it. The answer was to plan two counters at different heights, under two different qualities of light, rather than one dining set stranded in the middle of the floor.

The palette answers to the rest of the flat, the same white cabinetry set against stone and brass, though the lighting sits lower here and reads warmer. Everything below is a problem and the built response to it, which is why ourcommon space design servicestarts with counts and habits rather than with furniture.

The main table is marble topped on a slim profile, with the stone edge eased rather than bullnosed so it does not look heavier than it is. The chairs wear a warm neutral cloth pitched to agree with the brass rather than argue with it, and they are narrow enough across the back that an extra pair can be brought in from the breakfast bar when numbers rise. A round gold mirror on a marble panel faces the table from the side wall, which puts light back across the surface on days when the curtains at the far end are closed. Nothing on the table is fixed, so the room can be reset for a large gathering in about ten minutes.

A brass six arm chandelier centres over the table, and its outer arms were specified to finish inside the stone edge on both long sides. That measurement is worth more attention than it usually gets. A fixture that oversails the table looks wrong from every chair, and an undersized one drops the two end settings into gloom while the middle stays bright.

projects.title: Modular Kitchen Design in Basabo, Dhaka
projects.description:
The finish schedule was locked before the layout was. Grey handleless fronts through the working kitchen, an engineered stone top in a marble effect, grey stone tile to the walls, and one island dressed properly because the dining room can see it. Finishes in a Dhaka kitchen earn their place on how they clean, not on how they photograph. Grease films every surface within a month of handover, and the difference between a front you wipe and a front you scrub comes down to sheen level and edge detail. The room is really two rooms working together, an open island facing the dining table and a working galley behind it, and the sections below follow the order the whole thing was specified in, material by material.

Carcasses are moisture resistant board with sealed edges on every cut, including the ones nobody sees behind the plinth. Fronts are a matt grey with no handle at all, opening on a routed finger pull along the top edge, which in a galley this width means there is nothing to catch a sleeve or a dupatta on while carrying a hot pan.

The working run is L shaped and unbroken, and the appliance fronts are set flush into it so the elevation reads as one plane from wall to wall. Tall units are banked at the far end rather than spread along the length, which keeps the counter continuous instead of interrupted every couple of metres by a full height door. Ourmodular kitchen design servicebegins with a board schedule for exactly this reason, since a carcass chosen badly fails four years before the doors do.

The island top is marble taken as a waterfall, which means the slab turns down at both ends and runs to the floor rather than stopping at the counter line. The corners are mitred so the vein carries over the turn without a visible joint, which costs more to fabricate and is worth it on a piece this exposed. It is the surface that appears in almost every wide shot on the3,000 sq ft Basabo apartment project.

The working tops are engineered stone rather than natural marble, a deliberate downgrade in prestige and upgrade in behaviour, because turmeric, lime and hot oil mark real marble permanently and no sealer sold in Dhaka changes that. The walls behind the working run are grey stone tile in a large format, laid with the tightest grout joint the tile allows, so the splashback wipes down in one pass instead of needing a brush along every line.

projects.title: Luxury Master Bedroom Design in Basabo, Dhaka
projects.description:
You arrive in a corridor, not a bedroom. Both sides are lined with white classic wardrobe fronts running floor to ceiling, and a brass chandelier follows the centre of the ceiling above your head. The bed is already visible at the far end, framed by the opening where the corridor widens, so the suite reveals itself in two stages instead of all at once.

That staging was the plan rather than an accident of the shell. The master is three linked spaces, a dressing corridor, a sleeping area and a small lounge at the glazed end, which lets a couple keep different hours without either one turning on a main light. The suite sits at the quiet end of the3,000 sq ft Basabo apartment project, behind a pair of classic panelled doors that close it off from the corridor the children use.

The wardrobe fronts are a shaker profile in warm white, taken right up to the slab so there is no ledge on top to collect the dust that arrives through every Dhaka window. One section of the run is given over to open shelves for bags, lit from within, with the shelf pitch set to the tallest piece the run has to hold rather than to an even division of the opening. Those shelf lights are specified separately from the decorative chandelier and pitched close to neutral, because clothing chosen under warm light looks wrong the moment you step outside the flat. Internals were drawn against a written inventory of what has to be stored, sincebedroom interior design in Dhakaeither earns its fee inside the wardrobe or nowhere at all.

The corridor opens out where a full height mirror meets the return wall, and a vanity counter with a stool tucked beneath it fills the widened section. Putting the mirror at the widening rather than at the end means you stand with the room lit behind you and get a full length reflection, instead of a face lit hard from one side. The counter is deep enough to actually work at, with sockets set into the return so nothing trails across the surface, and it sits at a height that suits a seated user rather than splitting the difference with a standing one.

The stool is upholstered in the same neutral as the bed textiles and pushes fully under the counter, so the corridor stays clear when nobody is using it. Storage below the counter is drawers rather than doors, because a door swinging into a corridor width like this one is a daily irritation.

projects.title: Modern Boys Bedroom Design in Basabo, Dhaka
projects.description:
This room had to survive the gap between primary school and university without a rebuild. That single requirement rules out themes, colour blocking and anything scaled to a child, and it pushes the scheme toward fixed elements that stay neutral while the loose ones carry whatever personality the year happens to demand. Nothing built into these walls would embarrass a twenty year old.

Two further requirements shape the plan, storage and study, in that order. Clothing and sports kit go into a wardrobe wall that reaches the slab, homework goes into a dedicated nook, and the bed stands clear of both so the room never turns into a study with a bed pushed into the corner. It occupies the middle door on the children’s corridor in the3,000 sq ft Basabo apartment project, between the two other bedrooms.

The materials do the long term work. White panelling, brass fittings, grey drops at the window and a bed upholstered in brown. Those four will still read correctly when the room changes hands or changes purpose. Behind the bed, white fluting rises into a headboard panel, and above it hangs a circle built from overlapping mirror discs rather than one flat sheet, so the wall keeps some depth.

Everything in that group is joinery or metal. Nothing in it dates the way a printed wallpaper or a themed bedhead would. The upholstery on the bed is a mid brown in a hard wearing weave, chosen because it grounds an otherwise pale room and because it is the one surface in here that will take daily abuse for a decade. The base is a plain plinth with no visible feet, which keeps the floor line clean and stops the frame collecting whatever gets kicked under it.

Across the long wall the joinery is white panelled, with smoked glass on the centre pair of doors and fluting along the base. Smoked rather than clear was the right call for a teenager, since it shows the shape of what is inside without insisting that the inside be tidy. Interior shelves are lit, and the internals split between long hanging, short hanging and a deep drawer bank for sports kit, boots and the bag that would otherwise live on the floor. Appliance style flush facing was used on the door fronts, following the same rule about keeping an elevation flat that governs themodular kitchen design in Basabo.

projects.title: Modern Girls Bedroom Design in Basabo, Dhaka
projects.description:
In most Dhaka flats the smallest bedroom gets whatever furniture is left over from the rest of the house. This one absorbed more drawing hours than the master suite did, and the reason is simple arithmetic. Every centimetre a freestanding piece would have wasted here is a centimetre out of a room that had none to spare.

Colour was kept soft on purpose. Grey cloth on the headboard, joinery painted out in white, brushed gold on the handles and warm lamps throughout. The interest comes from shape and from hidden light rather than from pigment, which is the only approach that leaves a small room feeling larger finished than it did empty.

Set beside the3,000 sq ft Basabo apartment project, this is the clearest argument in the flat for planning the small rooms first. What follows puts each decision against the version you would usually get, including what had to be surrendered to make it work.

The conventional answer is a bought almirah, which leaves a dust shelf on top, a gap behind and a finish that never quite matches the room. Here it is white panelled joinery with slim gold handles, recessed into the wall depth and taken hard to the slab, so there is no wasted volume above and nothing to clean behind. Internally it splits between hanging and shelving in a ratio taken from what actually needed storing rather than from a standard. What was given up is flexibility. This wardrobe can never be moved, and its internals had to be settled months before anyone moved in, which is the part ofbedroom interior design in Dhakaclients find hardest to commit to.

The default for a daughter’s room in this city is a strong wall colour, usually pink, on at least one surface. A small room turns oppressive quickly under that treatment, so the walls stay white and the interest is carried by the arch over the bed and by light hidden behind the shelving.

projects.title: Luxury Guest Bedroom Design in Basabo, Dhaka
projects.description:
Quilted upholstered panelling carries the sconce on the wall opposite the bed, buttoned in a soft neutral and stretched over a padded backing that also deadens sound coming through from the corridor. It is the surface a guest looks at for a week, and it is the reason this room feels warmer than every other bedroom in the 3,000 sq ft flat around it. Spare rooms are usually the last drawn and the first to lose budget. This one was drawn in full, because a room used by visiting relatives for a week at a time several times a year is not a spare room in any useful sense. Of every room in the3,000 sq ft Basabo apartment projectit is the one carrying an actual picture on its wall, and the absence elsewhere was chosen rather than overlooked.

The quilting is a shallow diamond, buttoned rather than stitched through, on panels made to size in our workshop and hung on a batten so they can come off for cleaning. A lantern style sconce is mounted directly to one panel, with the fixing plate set into the frame behind the fabric so nothing pulls on the upholstery. The palette shifts warmer here on purpose, and a lantern in place of the plain brass tubes used elsewhere is part of that shift. It is switched twice, once at the door and once at the bedside. Double switching earns its cost here more than in any other room of a flat, because a visitor has no idea where anything is at two in the morning.

A landscape mural wallpaper runs behind the bed in muted greens and greys and turns the corner onto the return wall without a joint showing. Murals date fast when they are loud, so this one was picked for low contrast and behaves like texture from the doorway, resolving into a landscape only up close. A guest gets something to rest their eyes on, and nobody staying three nights has another household’s taste pushed at them. The forest niche in theluxury living room design in Basabodoes a similar job at a much smaller scale, framed inside an arch instead of running wall to wall.

Tall white doors with slim gold handles run the length of the far wall, and a lit display niche is let into the middle of the run for bags. The doors are a plain shaker with a narrow rail and they carry on right up to the slab, so the top of the run is a finished surface rather than a shelf for dust.

The internals are the part that matters. A guest wardrobe needs to take suitcases as much as clothing, so the base section is left clear and tall enough for a large case to stand upright with the lid opened, and the hanging space above is short rather than full drop. That niche runs off the room circuit and not a door contact, so no strip is left burning behind a shut door for a fortnight. Storage is exactly wherebedroom interior design in Dhakatends to go thin in a secondary room.

projects.title: Luxury Living Room Design in Bashundhara Block-L, Dhaka
projects.description:
Three zones, one floor plate, and not a single partition wall between them. Living, lounge and dining all sit on the same slab in this Bashundhara R/A Block-L flat, and dividing them was never on the table in a plan this open. Everything described below follows from that one restriction.

Marble is what solved it. The floor runs unbroken across all three zones with no threshold strip, and one wall of the main seating area is clad in the same stone from skirting to ceiling so the eye has somewhere to settle instead of hunting for a wall line. The rest of the palette stays deliberately quiet, beige on the upholstery and white on the joinery. This is the largest single space in the2,000 sq ft Bashundhara R/A Block-L apartment project.

An open grid shelf partition does the job a wall would have done and costs the room nothing in light. It is a slim frame loaded from both faces with plants and low objects, open enough that the lounge armchairs are visible straight through it from the sofa. Beige armchairs mark the lounge side. Behind them a mirrored panel wall runs floor to ceiling and returns the depth of the seating area back into itself, which counts for a lot in an apartment that takes daylight on one elevation only.

A second pair of dividers works the same way at the living room edge. Two planted glass shelf columns stand evenly either side of the sofa group, so from the front door the room reads as a defined rectangle even though nothing encloses it. A black coffee table between the sofas gives the pale scheme one hard dark object to sit against.

The full height marble accent wall behind the main seating faces the entry, so it is the first surface visible through the door. Two gold ring chandeliers hang in front of it rather than one central fitting, spaced to the sofa arrangement instead of centred on the ceiling. That came out of the furniture plan. A single large fixture would have landed off centre above a seating group that is not centred in the room, and it would have weighed on a ceiling working with standard slab height.

projects.title: Luxury Dining Room Design in Bashundhara Block-L, Dhaka
projects.description:
Slim gold legs under an oval marble top, and no corner anywhere on the table. That was the first thing decided in this dining room and the decision everything else answered to. The table stands at the busiest crossing point of a 2,000 sq ft flat in Bashundhara R/A Block-L, between the sofa group on one side and the kitchen counter on the other, so square corners would have cost circulation on both approaches. An oval also reads softer from the living room, which matters when the table is visible from the front door.

Marble flooring runs from the seating area to the kitchen threshold with no divider strip, and that continuity is what stops the dining zone looking marooned in the middle of an open plan. Against that floor the joinery is white, the chairs are tan and every metal item is gold. Three materials, and the room needs no fourth.

The top is a single oval slab with a shallow bevel worked into the edge, carried on four slim gold legs that meet the underside without an apron rail. Losing the apron was deliberate. An apron is what catches knees and stops a chair pushing fully under, and where the walking gap is this tight, sixty millimetres of tucked chair is worth having. Tan upholstered seats on gold frames continue the metal already in the room without introducing a fourth material to look after.

We size a table like this to the gap around it before we size it to the seat count, and that sequence sits at the centre of ourcommon space design service. The same brushed gold turns up again on the wardrobe pulls in theluxury master bedroom design in Bashundhara R/A Block-L, ordered from the same batch so the tone holds across rooms.

Behind the table a gold sunflower sculpture spreads across the wall in overlapping petals, roughly a metre and a half wide. It is the only large decorative object in the shared space and it earns that position by being legible from three different distances: from the sofa about six metres back, from a dining chair at arm’s length, and from the kitchen counter at an oblique angle. A cluster of smaller pieces fails that test. Fine detail vanishes at range, whereas the petals give a coarse silhouette from across the flat and a crisp edge up close.

projects.title: Modular Kitchen Design in Bashundhara Block-L, Dhaka
projects.description:
Step through the door and the island is straight ahead of you, a marble waterfall top on a fluted timber base with bar stools tucked along the near face. Beyond it the room opens into a U, grey shaker fronts on all three runs, gold handles on every door. A row of teardrop pendants hangs above the island at roughly eye level as you come in, which sets the height at which the whole room reads before you have taken a second step.

One door and one window fixed this layout before anything else could be decided. The U puts sink, hob and refrigerator on three separate runs with short walks between them, and it leaves the single window clear at the far end instead of building a tall unit across it. Everything below is described in the order you meet it walking in from that doorway. This kitchen and the dining zone on the other side of the counter make up the working half of the2,000 sq ft Bashundhara R/A Block-L apartment project.

The island top is marble effect surfacing with a mitred waterfall return down both ends, so the veining carries over the edge instead of stopping dead at a joint. Its base is fluted timber in a mid warm tone, the only wood in the room, cut from the same veneer family as the display column in theluxury master bedroom design in Bashundhara R/A Block-L. The overhang is set deep enough that a seated person’s knees clear the panel, a dimension missed more often than any other on an island, and it decides whether the stools get used or pushed aside.

Teardrop pendants hang in a row above, spaced to the stool positions rather than divided evenly along the island length. Those two spacings are almost never the same number. Following the stools is what stops one person eating in shadow while the person beside them sits under a lamp.

The tall run begins immediately to the right of the door. A built in oven sits at chest height with a microwave stacked above it, both housed in one grey tower that keeps the cabinet line unbroken so it reads as wall rather than as equipment. Nobody bends to load the oven, which across twenty years of daily cooking is a real saving on the back of whoever cooks most. Trays and baking tins go into deep drawers underneath.

projects.title: Luxury Master Bedroom Design in Bashundhara Block-L, Dhaka
projects.description:
The palette here is deliberately narrow: white and grey, wood permitted in exactly one place, gold used as a line and never as a mass. A room carrying this much fitted joinery cannot also carry a long material list, because every extra finish has to reappear somewhere else before it looks intentional. The single wood surface was kept large for the same reason, since one warm material only registers when it has enough area to work with.

That restriction is doing real work here, because this room carries more functions than any other in the flat. It sleeps, it stores an entire wardrobe, it holds a television, a built in desk and a full dressing station, and it opens onto a balcony. Ten materials would have turned it into a corridor of samples. Four keep it a bedroom. It is the largest of the four bedrooms in the2,000 sq ft Bashundhara R/A Block-L apartment project.

Every fixed element is finished in one white, sprayed lacquer over moisture resistant board rather than laminate, because the panelled profiles on the headboard wall and the wardrobe doors have return faces that a laminate sheet cannot follow around. The headboard wall is panelled from floor to ceiling with the bed centred on it and the nightstands sitting inside the panel field rather than alongside it. Both nightstands are wall hung, so the floor runs clear underneath them.

Carcass board was specified at eighteen millimetres with edge banding on every face including the concealed ones. Humidity in Dhaka moves through a cabinet interior in a way that an imported specification does not anticipate, and an unbanded internal edge is where a wardrobe begins to fail. The same standard governs the cabinetry in themodular kitchen design in Bashundhara R/A Block-L, where it is under even more pressure.

Gold appears in three places and nowhere else. Thin brass inlay strips, six millimetres wide, are set into the joints of the headboard panelling, so the wall picks up a bright line at every panel edge as light moves across it during the day. That detail is the whole reason the wall is not ordinary panelling, and it adds a small percentage to the panel cost rather than a large one. Long bar pulls on the wardrobe are the second use. The tall dressing mirror frame is the third.

projects.title: Modern Bedroom Design with Fluted Headboard in Bashundhara Block-L
projects.description:
One wall in this bedroom is decoration rather than architecture, and it is the only one doing that job. This is the smallest of the three secondary bedrooms in this Bashundhara R/A Block-L apartment, and it still had to take a full hanging wardrobe, a dressing position and a double bed without any of them touching. Floor area, not taste, is what set the approach. Concentrating the character budget on one vertical surface does more for a room this size than spreading the same money across four, so the wall behind the bed became a backlit fluted panel and the other three stood down. The room sits at the quiet end of the2,000 sq ft Bashundhara R/A Block-L apartment project.

The fluted panel is lit from its edges so the light grazes sideways across the ribs rather than pointing out into the room. Ribs are around thirty millimetres wide with a shallow radius and take the same white as the rest of the joinery, which means the pattern comes entirely from shadow and not from colour. In daylight the wall reads as texture. After dark it becomes the only light needed to cross the room, dimmed at the door.

A round marble disc hangs on that same wall and is the room’s single piece of art, its stone matched to the flooring used through theluxury living room design in Bashundhara R/A Block-L. One surface carrying this much of a room only works while the other three stay empty, which is why nothing else is hung above waist height apart from the dressing mirror.

Both nightstand tops had to stay clear, and in a room where the nightstand is barely wider than a paperback that is a requirement rather than a preference. Two gold ring pendants hang instead, one either side at bedside height, which empties both surfaces and removes two socket outlets from the skirting line. Drop height was fixed on site with the mattress in place rather than on the drawing, because the right height depends on mattress thickness and mattress thickness is the one dimension nobody confirms early enough.

Both pendants switch at the bed and again at the door, so the room can be crossed and shut down without anybody feeling along a wall in the dark. The rings are the same brushed gold as the fittings over the table in theluxury dining room design in Bashundhara R/A Block-L.
